name: AD — Directory Sync Account Sign-In From New Source
description: Companion to the DCSync detections. The Azure AD Connect sync account (MSOL_cb8d5eb8df87) is the one identity legitimately permitted to replicate directory secrets (Get-Changes-ALL). Over 90 days it authenticates from exactly one host — the AAD Connect server 10.11.18.16 (source.ip 100% populated). This rule (New Terms on source.ip, scoped to that account, 4624/4768) fires when the sync account authenticates from any OTHER source — i.e. its credentials/token were stolen and reused elsewhere. It closes the residual left by the Get-Changes-ALL rule, which allowlists the sync account: if the sync account itself is abused from a different host, this fires. Residual blind spot: abuse of the sync account FROM 10.11.18.16 itself (e.g. mimikatz on that server) produces no source novelty and requires host-level EDR on 10.11.18.16, which is not currently proven in NBI telemetry (recorded as a NO_TELEMETRY gap).
note:
### Triage — Azure AD Connect sync account from a new source
1. **WHO / to WHAT** `winlog.event_data.TargetUserName` = `MSOL_cb8d5eb8df87` (the directory-secret-capable sync account).
2. **FROM WHERE (discriminator)** `source.ip` — any value other than the canonical AAD Connect server `10.11.18.16`. This should never happen in normal operation.
3. **WHAT** 4624/4768 authentication (`event.code`, `winlog.logon.type`).
4. **Escalate:** treat as potential theft of the AAD Connect account. Correlate with the Get-Changes-ALL rule — if this account also replicated secrets from the new host, it is an active DCSync. First rule out a legitimate AAD Connect server migration/failover that changed the IP.

standard.logic_explanation: New Terms on source.ip for the AAD Connect account's 4624/4768; fires on a source IP other than 10.11.18.16.
standard.residual_gap: abuse from 10.11.18.16 itself needs host EDR (NO_TELEMETRY)
